findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised instance unrestricted outbound connectivity for data exfiltration or C2 traffic.

AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in the EC2 user_data script; user data is retrievable via the instance metadata service and stored in plaintext in state, leaking long-lived credentials.
The instance does not configure root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root volume data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, leaving IMDSv1 enabled and the instance vulnerable to credential theft via SSRF.
The instance is launched in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a wide-open security group, giving it a public IP directly reachable from the internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data written to the attached disk is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the backup copy of the data is also stored unencrypted and could be exposed if shared or copied.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network telemetry is stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy restrictions are defined for the flow log bucket, risking accidental public exposure of network logs.

findings.issue_category: missing versioning and force destroy enabled
findings.description: force_destroy = true allows the audit-log bucket and all flow log objects to be deleted without protection, and no versioning is configured, undermining log integrity.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, automatically expanding internet-facing attack surface.
